reviewMethod: Fresh answerless browser-effective worksheet; prior authoring conclusions and remembered keys treated as non-evidence; all independent answers and verdicts completed before keyed reconciliation.

g5s-cr-001.value: The evidence supports conservation of matter because the sealed bag was 100 g before and after dissolving. The tablet's matter did not disappear when it became invisible; it remained in the solution inside the sealed bag.

g5s-cr-002.value: The stronger push produced a greater change in motion. The identical car pushed with 3 N traveled 118 cm, while the car pushed with 1 N traveled only 45 cm under the same conditions.

g5s-cr-003.value: Matter can move from air and water into grass, then to a rabbit that eats the grass, and later into a fox that eats the rabbit. Decomposers break down wastes and dead organisms and return matter to soil and air, where producers can use it again.

g5s-cr-004.value: The claim that the added plant material came chiefly from soil should be rejected. The plant gained 18 g of dry mass, while the soil lost only 4 g, so soil cannot account for most of the gain. The plant also had access to air and water, which supply most of the materials used to build new plant matter.

g5s-cr-005.value: Soil loss increased as slope increased: 11 g on the nearly flat tray, 25 g on the medium slope, and 44 g on the steep tray. The data therefore support that steeper slopes had more soil moved by runoff under these test conditions.

g5s-cr-006.value: Repairing the leaks appears to reduce water use: average daily outdoor use fell from 920 L to 610 L, a reduction of 310 L per day. A stronger comparison would measure water use for more matched days while also recording conditions such as rainfall or irrigation need.
